content: Rifapentine has the potential to reduce the levels or effectiveness of various medications by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10. This interaction accelerates the metabolism of these drugs, leading to decreased plasma concentrations and potentially reduced therapeutic efficacy. Below is a detailed explanation of the interactions: 1. Estradiol Vaginal, Conjugated Estrogens, Esterified Estrogens, and Estropipate: Rifapentine decreases their levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Eszopiclone: Rifapentine reduces its levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitoring is advised. 3. Ethosuximide and Ethotoin: Rifapentine decreases their levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism, respectively. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Etonogestrel and Etoposide: Rifapentine reduces their levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 5. Etravirine: Rifapentine decreases its levels by inducing both CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 enzymes. Monitoring is advised. 6. Exemestane: Rifapentine reduces its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. For patients on potent CYP3A4 inducers, the recommended dose of exemestane is 50 mg daily after a meal. 7. Felbamate and Felodipine: Rifapentine decreases their levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 8. Fentanyl (all forms): Rifapentine reduces fentanyl levels, potentially leading to withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may increase fentanyl plasma concentrations, necessitating close monitoring for respiratory depression. 9. Fesoterodine and Flibanserin: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. 10. Fludrocortisone and Fosamprenavir: Rifapentine reduces their levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 11. Fosaprepitant and Fosphenytoin: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism, respectively. Caution is advised. 12. Gefitinib: Rifapentine reduces its levels. Increase gefitinib to 500 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers, and resume the standard dose 7 days after discontinuing the inducer. 13. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Rifapentine decreases their plasma concentrations, potentially reducing therapeutic effects. Monitoring is required. 14. Glimepiride, Glipizide, and Glyburide: Rifapentine reduces their levels by increasing metabolism. Strong CYP2C9 inducers may further enhance glyburide metabolism. 15. Guanfacine: Rifapentine significantly reduces guanfacine plasma concentrations and half-life. For ADHD patients, consider doubling the dose of extended-release guanfacine. 16. Haloperidol and Hydrocodone: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 17. Hydrocortisone and Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Rifapentine reduces their levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 18. Ifosfamide: Rifapentine increases its toxicity by enhancing the formation of neurotoxic and nephrotoxic metabolites. Close monitoring for toxicities is essential. 19. Iloperidone and Imipramine: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 20. Indinavir and Ixabepilone: Rifapentine reduces their levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised. 21. Lapatinib and Lesinurad: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism, respectively. Monitoring is necessary. 22. Levonorgestrel (all forms): Rifapentine reduces its levels, potentially compromising contraceptive efficacy. Use alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after rifapentine use. 23. Linagliptin: Rifapentine reduces its levels. Alternative treatments are strongly recommended when co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. 24. Lomitapide and Lopinavir: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 25. Loratadine and Losartan: Rifapentine reduces their levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism, respectively. Monitoring is advised. 26. Maraviroc and Marijuana: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is necessary. 27. Medroxyprogesterone and Mefloquine: Rifapentine reduces their levels, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 28. Mestranol and Methadone: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 29. Methylprednisolone and Metoprolol: Rifapentine reduces their levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 30. Midazolam and Mifepristone: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with mifepristone is not recommended. 31. Mirtazapine and Modafinil: Rifapentine reduces their levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 32. Nateglinide and Nelfinavir: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. Caution is necessary. 33. Nevirapine and Nicardipine: Rifapentine reduces their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 34. Nifedipine and Nilotinib: Rifapentine decreases their levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 35. Nisoldipine and Norgestrel: Rifapentine reduces their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider additional barrier contraception methods. 36. Oliceridine and Osilodrostat: Rifapentine decreases their levels. Adjust doses as needed and monitor for withdrawal symptoms or therapeutic effects. 37. Ospemifene and Oxycodone: Rifapentine reduces their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 38. Paclitaxel (all forms): Rifapentine decreases its levels, potentially reducing efficacy. Monitoring is necessary. 39. Parecoxib and Pazopanib: Rifapentine reduces their levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. Monitoring is advised. 40. Phenytoin and Pimavanserin: Rifapentine decreases their levels. Avoid co-administration with pimavanserin if possible. 41. Pitolisant and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Rifapentine reduces their levels. Adjust doses as needed and monitor for therapeutic effects. 42. Prednisolone and Prednisone: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 43. Primaquine and Propranolol: Rifapentine reduces their levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 44. Quazepam and Quetiapine: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 45. Quinidine and Repaglinide: Rifapentine reduces their levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 46. Ribociclib and Rifabutin: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 47. Riociguat and Ritonavir: Rifapentine reduces their levels. Data for dose adjustment is unavailable. 48. Ruxolitinib (all forms): Rifapentine decreases its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 49. Selexipag and Sildenafil: Rifapentine reduces their levels. Adjust selexipag doses as needed. 50. Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Rifapentine decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora. Monitoring is advised. 51. Solifenacin and Sorafenib: Rifapentine reduces their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 52. Sufentanil and Sunitinib: Rifapentine decreases their levels. Monitor for withdrawal symptoms or therapeutic effects. 53. Suvoxerant and Tacrolimus: Rifapentine reduces their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 54. Tadalafil and Tamoxifen: Rifapentine decreases their levels. Avoid combination in pulmonary hypertension patients. 55. Tamsulosin and Tasimelteon: Rifapentine reduces their levels. Avoid co-administration with tasimelteon. 56. Temsirolimus and Teniposide: Rifapentine decreases their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 57. Terbinafine and Tetracycline: Rifapentine reduces their levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. Monitoring is necessary. 58. Theophylline and Tiagabine: Rifapentine decreases their levels. Adjust therapy as needed. 59. Ticagrelor and Tinidazole: Rifapentine reduces their levels. Avoid ticagrelor with potent CYP3A4 inducers. 60. Tipranavir and Tofacitinib: Rifapentine decreases their levels. Monitor for therapeutic effects. 61. Tolterodine and Toremifene: Rifapentine reduces their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 62. Tramadol and Triamcinolone: Rifapentine decreases their levels. Monitor for therapeutic effects. 63. Triazolam and Vardenafil: Rifapentine reduces their levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 64. Verapamil and Vilazodone: Rifapentine decreases their levels. Monitoring is advised. In summary, rifapentine significantly impacts the metabolism of numerous drugs, primarily through CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 induction. Close monitoring, dose adjustments, or alternative therapies may be required to maintain therapeutic efficacy and avoid adverse effects.
